<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `39b1863604d9a0b96eac60244acabdf1d6daaa34` — the merge of head `b9ae58bf897d3a4fad458875463128305327c691` into base `a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 39b1863604d9a0b96eac60244acabdf1d6daaa34 && git checkout 39b1863604d9a0b96eac60244acabdf1d6daaa34
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3 b9ae58bf897d3a4fad458875463128305327c691 && git checkout -B drift-repro a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3 && git merge --no-ff b9ae58bf897d3a4fad458875463128305327c691

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1: REWORK, one item** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `44b4972c7538290118112717012810377cafebb4`, read 2026-11-20T04:07Z. Everything else below already reads ACCEPT. A delta L1 on the new head closes this.

### Must fix

1. **Pin the two skips the changeset ships beyond `afterUpdate`.** The changeset tells app authors "no roll-up recomputes and no record-changed event is published". `engine-update.ts` implements both: `if (this.realtimeService && !noOpUpdate)`, and `summaryFailures = noOpUpdate ? [] : …` plus the `summaryKeyColumns` read guard. But no test in this PR, and none I found on main, would go red if either were lost. The new file boots without a `realtimeService` and declares no roll-up. Add, in `engine-update-all-dropped-noop-34746.test.ts`:
   - **Event pin.** A stub realtime service on the kernel. On an all-dropped update, by-id and predicate each publish no `updated` event. Control: the surviving-field case publishes exactly one (by-id `data.record.updated`, predicate the bulk event).
   - **Roll-up pin.** A parent with a summary over this object. An all-dropped child update leaves the parent unwritten and calls no recompute, on both branches. Control: the surviving-field case still recomputes.
   - **Ablation.** Re-run the ablation with each of the two guards forced off on its own, and quote the red/green counts in the PR body like the existing one.

   Why REWORK and not a note: these two lines are behaviour an app can observe, and the changeset tells authors about them. Under `l1-review-checklist.md`, a stated behaviour needs a test that fails without it; green output from the existing pins does not cover them.

### Read and accepted (carries over to the delta)

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #34746` is the only closing keyword, and it fits once the pins land. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` and `Skills-docs: follow-up #35605` sit at line start. #35605 is open, `domain:skills`, and `pm:blocked` on this work.
- **Changeset.** `'@objectstack/objectql': minor` is right for `semantic`, under AGENTS.md step 3. The "What to check in an app" migration line is present. Prose checked against the diff: "no driver write … answers the current record … `0` rows written … dropped fields still reported … `beforeUpdate` still runs … a surviving field (caller or `beforeUpdate`-written) takes the unchanged path … same-value write unchanged … `strictReadonlyWrites` still refuses first". Each sentence matches the code and a pin, except the event and roll-up sentence, which is item 1.
- **Code.** `everyCallerKeyDropped`:
  - It is asked after both read-only strips, on both branches.
  - It returns `false` when there is an ADR-0142 precondition, an empty payload (address aside), a key not taken by a strip (a hook-deleted key included), or a non-stamp key left (a `beforeUpdate`-written key included).
  - `reportDroppedFields` now records drops with no listener, and still emits only to a listener or strict mode.
  - Validation, the post-image seam and reference checks still run before the verdict is used, so earlier refusals keep answering.
  - The by-id answer `{ ...priorRecord }` is the not-found gate's own read (`readUpdatePriorRow`, declared columns, the caller's driver options), so there is no second fetch. It then passes through `stripSearchCompanion` like a written row.
  - I found no `afterUpdate` hook that shapes the returned record (masking is not on that chain), so skipping the chain exposes nothing new.
- **The point d7-B raised: the extension beyond the card text.** Accepted in substance. The card's goal is that a change-nothing update is not treated as an edit by automation. The realtime event is the other automation channel, and a roll-up over an unchanged row moves nothing. The changeset discloses both. Only the missing pins (item 1) hold this.
- **The four edited test files.** Accepted. Each pin's payload was all-dropped before, so the new rule would have turned it into a no-op. Adding one writable field keeps the pin on the strip it was written for: the `dropped` event assertions are unchanged, and each now also asserts the surviving key reached the driver. The two `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` rows register the new `updated_at` / `updated_by` literals as `not-a-read` vocabulary, which is what that ledger is for.
- **Tests and ablation.** 10 cases through the real `ObjectQLPlugin` stamp hook. Base reading: 7/10 red. Guard-off ablation: 5 defect cases red and 5 controls green, restored blob-equal. Refusal pin (strict): `fields` asserted and nothing written.
- **Gates.** CI at `44b4972c`: 57 check runs, 39 `success` and 18 `skipped`, none red. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` are `success`.
- **Contract review (L2).** None owed by face (`contract-review.md`): no `Clause-②: yes`, no `(narrowing)` arm, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path. The declaration is right: nothing the engine accepted is now refused (the write still answers, and drops are reported as before). The change is to when the write and its hooks happen, which is `Metadata-protocol: semantic` and a `minor`, not a narrowing. The card's "L1 + L2 + Tier H" line was the filing seat's reading, and it does not bind. Tier follows the governed path set (SKILL.md 〈路径分叉〉), and this PR has none, so it is non-governed and lands by the area after `check-governed-merges` and a green delta ACCEPT.
- **Noted, not filed.** The `__search` and `updated_at`-only cases in `## Acceptance notes`: unchanged behaviour, agreed.

## Patch round 1: event and roll-up pins

This answers L1 comment 7030108475 at new head `b9ae58bf8`. It is a test-only commit. `engine-update.ts` is byte-identical to `44b4972c7` (blob `215cfc4e`).

`engine-update-all-dropped-noop-34746.test.ts` now runs 18 cases (it had 10). The stub driver now keeps one store per object, and the existing 10 cases are unchanged.

- **Event pin.** A stub realtime service is set on the engine (`setRealtimeService`).
  - On an all-dropped update, by-id and predicate each publish no `nd_task` `*.updated` event.
  - Controls: a surviving field publishes exactly one `data.record.updated` (by-id) and exactly one `data.records.updated` (predicate).
- **Roll-up pin.** A parent `nd_project` carries a `count` summary over `nd_line` (`master_detail`). Its stored count is a deliberately stale 99, with two lines.
  - On an all-dropped line update, by-id and predicate each leave the parent unwritten: no driver write to `nd_project`, and `line_count` 99, `updated_at` and `updated_by` stay as seeded.
  - Controls: a surviving field recomputes the parent to 2, on both branches.

Run on the new head: `Tests 18 passed (18)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` gave exit 0. `check:objectql-double-limit`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:nul-bytes` and `check:engine-double-contract` each gave exit 0.

### Ablations

All ablations went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each mutation landed on disk (anchor 1 to 0), and each run restored to HEAD blob `215cfc4ea660` with `git diff HEAD` empty.

| Guard forced off | Result | Red |
|---|---|---|
| No-op guard (`everyCallerKeyDropped` forced false), round 0 | 5 failed, 5 passed (10) | the 5 defect cases |
| **Event skip** (`if (this.realtimeService && !noOpUpdate)` becomes `if (this.realtimeService)`) | **1 failed, 17 passed (18)** | by-id: no updated event |
| **Roll-up skip**, both lines (`summaryKeyColumns.length > 0 && !noOpUpdate` and `summaryFailures = noOpUpdate ? [] : …`) | **2 failed, 16 passed (18)** | by-id and predicate: parent unwritten |
| Roll-up skip, the `summaryFailures` ternary alone | 1 failed, 17 passed (18) | by-id: parent unwritten |

What the table shows about the predicate event pin: it stays green with the event guard off. A predicate no-op answers `0`, and `publishBulkDataEvent` already publishes nothing for `matched === 0` (`engine-realtime-publish.ts`: "a predicate that matched nothing changed no data"). So on that branch the pin is held by the no-op's zero count, and the event guard is load-bearing for the by-id branch only. The pin still states the shipped behaviour on both branches.

On the predicate roll-up, both lines must go before it reds. The `summaryKeyColumns` guard only skips the pre-write read, and the recompute itself is skipped by the `summaryFailures` ternary.

**L1 delta: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `b9ae58bf897d3a4fad458875463128305327c691`, read 2026-11-20T04:37Z. This closes REWORK 7030108475. That comment's "read and accepted" items carry over.

Delta: one test-only commit (`b9ae58bf`, parent `44b4972c`), one file. `packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts` is byte-identical (blob `215cfc4e` at both heads), so code, changeset and declarations are unchanged from the first read.

- **Item 1 is met.** `engine-update-all-dropped-noop-34746.test.ts` now runs 18 cases.
  - **Event pin.** A stub service is set through `setRealtimeService`. An all-dropped update publishes no `*.updated` event for the object, on by-id and on predicate. Controls: a surviving field publishes exactly one `data.record.updated` (by-id) and exactly one `data.records.updated` (predicate).
  - **Roll-up pin.** A `master_detail` line under a parent with a `count` summary, seeded stale at 99. An all-dropped line update leaves the parent with no driver write and `line_count`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` as seeded, on both branches. Controls: a surviving field recomputes the parent to 2, on both branches.
- **Ablations, per guard** (dev comment 7030474653): event skip off ⇒ 1 red; both roll-up skip lines off ⇒ 2 red; the `summaryFailures` ternary alone ⇒ 1 red. Each was restored blob-equal. The counts are in a PR comment instead of the body. Accepted: the comment is on the PR and pinned to this head.
- **The dev's note on the predicate event pin, verified.** `publishBulkDataEvent` in `engine-realtime-publish.ts` returns early on `matched === 0` ("a predicate that matched nothing changed no data"). So once the no-op answers `0`, that branch publishes nothing, with or without the `!noOpUpdate` guard. The guard is load-bearing on by-id, which ablation shows red. The predicate pin still states the shipped behaviour, held by the zero answer. Likewise, the `summaryKeyColumns … && !noOpUpdate` guard only skips the pre-write read; the recompute skip is the `summaryFailures` ternary, which is pinned on both branches. Both readings match the code.
- **Harness change.** The stub driver now keeps one store per object, and `rows` / `writes` stay the task object's own. So the existing 10 cases assert exactly what they did before (`writes` records only `OBJECT`), and the new cases read other objects through `writesTo` / `storeFor`.
- **Gates.** CI at `b9ae58bf`: 53 check runs, 37 `success` and 16 `skipped`, none red or pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` are `success`.

**Contract review.** None owed (no L2 face; see 7030108475). This PR is non-governed and +533/−37 is under 3,000 lines, so it lands by the area after `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35594`.
